patch.value: Generate default changelog heading dates in UTC

The core generator derives an omitted release date with local Date calendar fields, so the same instant produces different changelog bytes in UTC and Europe/Vienna. This broke pm-vcs PR #6 after local midnight and blocks safe fleet adoption of pm-changelog 2026.7.29.

A frozen instant whose UTC and Europe/Vienna calendar dates differ generates byte-identical headings under both timezones; The default heading date is the UTC YYYY-MM-DD date; Explicit --date and tag-derived date behavior remains unchanged; Prepend replace stdout release-notes and check paths inherit the same core policy; README and CLI help document the UTC fallback; Strict release check and installed CLI acceptance pass
pm-changelog main at 28b25b8; Europe/Vienna just after midnight while UTC remains the previous date
At an instant such as 2026-08-01T22:30:00Z set TZ=UTC and generate without --date, then set TZ=Europe/Vienna and regenerate. The old generator emits 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-02 respectively.
The same clock instant and PM data produce identical changelog bytes on every host, defaulting the generated calendar date to UTC.
The default date uses getFullYear/getMonth/getDate and therefore depends on the process timezone.
Fleet changelog checks fail nondeterministically near midnight and block otherwise valid PRs and releases.
